findings.summary: pip would incorrectly handle doubly-encoded package URLs from indexes
findings.exposure: Disposable venv bootstrap/package-install tooling, not application runtime.
findings.applicable_usage: Requires malicious index; auditing used explicit trusted PyPI. Repository CI already upgrades pip and the CI-aligned target resolved patched 26.3.
findings.provisional_remediation_type: Upgrade disposable/CI bootstrap pip to patched release; no application manifest change.
findings.final_remediation_type: Both Python CI jobs use bounded patched bootstrap pip>=26.2,<27; latest tested26.3. Explicit>=3.11 support policy avoids unsupported3.9 tool resolution.

findings.exposure: Development/test only; local UNIX predictable temporary-directory handling.
findings.applicable_usage: Tests run on disposable controlled CI/local environments; no production pytest use. Fixed 9.0.3 requires Python >=3.10 while project still declares >=3.9.
findings.provisional_remediation_type: Retain explicit medium residual until Python floor/test-major compatibility decision; no patched 8.x release available in current PyPI metadata. Isolate temporary directories and avoid untrusted shared local test execution.
findings.final_remediation_type: Upgrade to >=9.0.3,<9.1 after explicitly raising both service Python minimums to>=3.11; run complete regressions and advisory audit. No current medium-risk retention.

findings.exposure: Disposable venv bootstrap/build tooling; low severity Windows-only legacy wheel installation path.
